briefFidelity: FAIL on the brief's two load-bearing clauses. (1) 'the drawing carried in fine line so the whole reads as engineering rather than as mass' — my blind description reached independently for the exact word the brief forbids: I wrote 'filled with a translucent desaturated slate blue-grey', 'overlaps read as tonal steps', 'collapse into a single flat grey blob', 'flattens toward a single soft grey mass'. This collection is built almost entirely from filled translucent area. Stroke appears only as an occasional gold contour (9011 recovery, 9190's inner hexagon) and as two annuli; nothing is drawn in fine line, and nothing reads as engineering. (2) 'Under volatility the mechanism should loosen — its members spreading apart and the rings separating — and tighten again as conditions settle' — the shipped transformation is a different axis, run backwards (see marketResponse). What the brief DOES get: brass and slate over a dark ground is exact and unprompted; no gear teeth, hands, numerals or dial markings appear anywhere; and tokens genuinely differ in order of rotational symmetry (three-, four- and six-fold) and in ring count. But 'radial members' are absent as such — there are no spokes, struts or arms anywhere in the twelve, only detached satellite blobs orbiting at a radius — and 'the regularity of something machined' is contradicted by the jittered, clumped tokens (9727, 10264, 10622, 10801, 10980) and by orphan gold satellites flung out toward the frame corner with nothing connecting them to the body. Because briefFidelity is a gate, this alone forecloses PASS.
seedVariation: ACCEPTABLE — the one axis this collection clearly delivers. On the 120px sheet the twelve are recognisably one family (centred, three-note palette, nested, radial) while roughly nine or ten remain individually identifiable: the six-satellite snowflake (9190), the bullseye (9906), the gold-rimmed bubble field (9369), the bitten circle with its corona (9548), the chaotic gold cluster (9727), the gold diamond (10443), the gold-outlined triple (10264). It is neither twelve unrelated works nor one work twelve times. The weak end is real but not fatal: 9011, 10622 and 10801 all reduce to 'grey hexagon, faint interior, one gold speck' and cannot be told apart at browse size, and 10264 and 10980 nearly converge.
thumbnailSurvival: PARTIAL. Silhouette survives well — hexagon, circle and diamond are unambiguous at 120px and the satellite ring reads as a bumped or spiky edge. Gold survives as a rim, contour or speck and is doing most of the differentiating work. What does not survive is the nesting: the interior translucent shapes merge into one flat value in the plainer tokens, which is precisely the failure mode the brief's 'fine line' instruction exists to prevent — line survives downscaling, low-contrast translucent fill does not. Three of twelve become mutually indistinguishable.
marketResponse: VISIBLE BUT NOT THE CLAIMED CHANGE, AND INVERTED. The change is large and unmistakable even at browse size, so this does not fail for being invisible — it fails for being a different transformation. What I recorded blind was amplitude and ornament, not spacing: stress contracts the body, strips the gold almost completely (9369 loses its entire rim and shrinks, 9190's satellites shrink to grey stubs, 9548's corona vanishes outright) and flattens the whole toward a single soft grey mass; recovery inflates the form and floods gold back in heavier than neutral (9011 gains a bold gold outline it never had, 9369's rim becomes a thick saturated annulus, 9548 grows a denser corona than neutral). The brief asks for loosening under volatility — members spreading apart, rings separating — and tightening as conditions settle. Stress is the tightest, smallest, most collapsed state in every one of the four tokens; recovery is the largest and most spread. Even reading the size change generously as 'looseness', it is mapped backwards at both ends. Rings do not separate under stress; they disappear.
tokenIdentity: PASS, and the strongest result on the sheet. Across all three rows each token is unmistakably the same object: 9011 keeps its nested hexagon, 9369 keeps four inner bubbles in identical relative positions, 9190 keeps its six stations, 9548 keeps its dark bite at the lower left and its overall mass. Nothing morphs into a different primitive or reshuffles its interior. Whatever the mapping is doing wrong, it is doing it to a stable object.
composition: Focal hierarchy is clean and unambiguous — one dominant centred mass, generous margin, no competition for attention, dark ground held consistently. But the frame is barely used: every token floats at roughly half to two-thirds of the tile with no edge relationship, so the format is passive rather than composed. Two real artifacts: orphan satellites detached from the body by large empty gaps (10622, 10801, 10980 each carry one or two gold hexagons stranded near a corner with nothing linking them to the form), which read as debris rather than as members of a mechanism; and 10980's lower-right satellite sits hard against the tile corner. Mush is confined to the interiors of the plainer tokens at 120px rather than affecting silhouettes.
reasoning: Writing blind, before I knew what had been asked for, I described translucent filled masses whose overlaps read as tonal steps and which flatten at browse size into a single grey blob — and I described a condition axis of contraction-and-stripping under stress against inflation-and-gilding under recovery. The brief asks for the opposite of both: a mechanism carried in fine line so it reads as engineering rather than as mass, which loosens and separates under volatility and tightens as conditions settle. Two of the brief's three sentences are therefore not delivered, and the one that is delivered — brass and slate over a dark ground, no literal escapement parts, varying symmetry order and ring count — is the palette-and-inventory sentence rather than the sentence that says what the thing should be. The craft is not the problem: token identity holds firmly, seed variation is genuine, the silhouettes read at 120px, and the transformation is boldly visible. But this is a permanent on-chain commitment, and what would be committed is a set of soft nested blobs whose response to the market runs backwards against its own stated behaviour. A viewer told this loosens under volatility would watch it clench instead. That is a claimed transformation contradicted by the art, on top of a failed fidelity gate, and either one is sufficient to refuse.
wouldChange: Redraw the whole collection in stroke rather than fill — rings and members as fine brass and slate line work on the dark ground, with interiors open. That is the brief's central instruction, it is upstream of everything else here (line survives 120px where low-contrast translucent fill does not, and separation between rings is only legible once the rings are drawn as rings rather than as stacked discs), and it converts the orphan satellites into connectable members instead of debris. Then, mandatorily and second: invert the condition mapping so stress spreads the members and opens the ring spacing while recovery draws them back in — the current mapping is not merely unclaimed, it is the reverse of what the brief states.
